bull_bear.body:
- Diversified customer base of over 50 OEMs and Tier-1 companies with long-standing relationships (TAFE, Tata Motors, DANA, Ashok Leyland, Escorts, Automotive Axles Limited, Meritor, American Axles & Manufacturing), validated by supplier awards such as 'Best in Class Supplier', 'Best Delivery Performance' and 'Platinum Award for Best Quality'
- Strategic manufacturing location 37-140 km from Chennai (a major automotive hub and steel-scrap source) and 15-110 km from India's largest silica sand source near Gudur, with proximity to Chennai's international airport and Krishnapatnam & Chennai seaports supporting exports
- Strong export growth potential as one of few Indian foundries capable of meeting requirements of top global OEMs and Tier-1 manufacturers; exports contributed about 29% of FY26 turnover (Rs 384.91 crore)
- Differentiated product mix, having transitioned from basic products to medium-to-high complexity castings, supporting higher margins and competitive positioning against local and Chinese low-complexity suppliers
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Economy and market (cyclicality) risk — External factors such as government policies and rainfall can significantly impact Tractor and Commercial Vehicle sales, which are cyclical in nature; the Company mitigates this by developing export segments and other segments such as off-highway and railways.
- Input cost risk — Profitability and cost-effectiveness may be affected by changes in prices of raw materials, power and other input costs; the Company is typically able to pass these costs to customers only with a slight lag, and this risk is flagged as significant and carefully monitored.
- Currency risk — Foreign-currency exposure arises primarily through export earnings and the import of some capital goods and raw materials; exposure is typically short term, and the Company does selective hedging of imports/exports and fully hedges any substantial long-term liabilities such as ECBs.
- Interest rate risk — The Company is exposed to interest rate risk on funds borrowed from banks and works closely with its banks to minimise overall interest costs through effective use of working capital.
- Export revenue concentration — Exports contributed about 29% of FY26 turnover (Rs 384.91 crore), concentrated in North America, Europe and Southeast Asia, exposing the Company to overseas demand cycles, tariff and trade-policy shifts in those markets.
- Regulatory / emission-norms risk — Evolving emission and safety norms -- including TREM V norms for tractors and measures such as mandatory air-conditioned cabins for commercial vehicles -- may raise vehicle costs and affect near-term demand and tractor pricing, even though they are expected to support long-term sector modernisation.
- Macro and commodity-price volatility risk — Management's outlook flags risks from volatility in raw material prices (particularly steel scrap and energy costs), geopolitical uncertainties, fluctuations in freight and logistics costs, subdued monsoon and potential supply chain disruptions as factors that could affect performance despite a broadly positive demand outlook.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Nelcast manufactures ductile and grey iron castings (0.5 kg to 500 kg), including Grey Iron, Ductile Iron and Austempered Ductile Iron, for Commercial Vehicle, Tractor, Off-Highway Equipment, Railways and Passenger Vehicle OEMs and Tier-1 customers. The Company deals in a single reportable segment, Iron Castings, and sells to a diversified base of over 50 customers including TAFE, Tata Motors, DANA, Ashok Leyland, Escorts, Automotive Axles Limited, Meritor and American Axles & Manufacturing, with a growing export presence across North America, Europe and Southeast Asia.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Clear strategic focus on enhancing operational efficiency, increasing the share of value-added products, deepening customer relationships, and building a more resilient financial and operational foundation
- Operational excellence as a central strategic theme: productivity enhancement, process optimisation, automation, energy efficiency and cost management initiatives across facilities
- Expanding capabilities in large and complex castings, particularly for commercial vehicle and tractor applications, leveraging engineering and manufacturing strengths for competitive advantage
- Sustainability positioned as an integral part of long-term strategy, with continued pursuit of renewable energy and sustainability performance improvements alongside disciplined capital allocation
- Continued new product development and disciplined operational focus to capitalise on emerging domestic and export opportunities
- Diversifying into export segments and other end-markets (off-highway, railways) to mitigate the cyclicality/seasonality risk inherent in the domestic tractor and commercial vehicle market
- Sustained focus on technology and quality while offering a wide range of products to diversified segments and customers to maintain competitive edge
- Declaration of a dividend for FY26 is listed as ordinary business at the AGM (per the Notice to Shareholders). The Company maintains a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy framed in accordance with Regulation 43A of the SEBI LODR Regulations, referenced under the 'Dividend Distribution Policy' section and made available on the Company's website. No further capital-allocation policy detail (e.g., buyback, reinvestment philosophy) is disclosed in this bundle.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company secured several new business wins during FY26 that are expected to support a significant ramp-up of the Pedapariya (Andhra Pradesh) facility in the upcoming year; a number of these products have completed customer validation and will move into production in the coming months, marking a shift toward higher-value, more technically complex products. Management also states more broadly that the Company has made significant investments to increase capacity, positioning it to benefit from growth in both the domestic automotive industry and global markets, though no specific project names, dates or rupee quantum for this broader capacity investment are disclosed in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Domestic demand remained robust through FY26, particularly in the medium and heavy commercial vehicle and tractor segments, supporting improved capacity utilisation across manufacturing facilities
- Export markets were subdued for a significant part of FY26 due to uncertainty around US tariffs, causing many US truck buyers to defer fleet replacement decisions; a gradual recovery emerged toward year-end as tariff and emission-norm clarity improved
- Order visibility indicates export recovery is expected to continue through 2026, driven by pre-buy activity ahead of upcoming emission-related regulatory changes
- EBITDA per kilogram improvement attributed to a better product mix, improved operating leverage and sustained cost optimisation initiatives
- Commercial vehicle segment demand supported by GST reductions, increased infrastructure activity, improved fleet utilisation and better replacement demand
- Tractor demand supported by a good monsoon, GST rate reductions and agricultural activity
- For FY27, domestic demand (particularly commercial vehicle) is expected to remain supportive while export markets show encouraging signs of recovery
- Industry-wide: Commercial Vehicle segment recorded its highest-ever domestic sales (10.80 lakh units, +12.6%), supported by infrastructure activity, replacement demand and improved freight/financing conditions, expected to support continued demand for castings and auto components
- M&HCV segment continues to benefit from ageing-fleet replacement demand, improving freight utilisation and sustained infrastructure investment
- Domestic tractor industry achieved record sales exceeding 1 million units in FY26 (+23.47% YoY), supported by favourable monsoon, higher MSPs, improved rural liquidity and government support; growth is expected to normalise in FY27 on a higher base while remaining supported by rural fundamentals and mechanisation trends
- Outlook remains subject to risks from raw material price volatility (steel scrap, energy costs), geopolitical uncertainty, freight/logistics cost fluctuations, subdued monsoon, exchange rate movements and potential supply chain disruptions
- Evolving emission and safety norms (including TREM V for tractors) and regulatory requirements such as mandatory air-conditioned cabins may raise near-term costs but are expected to support long-term sector modernisation
- Several new business wins secured during FY26 are expected to support a significant ramp-up of the Pedapariya facility in the upcoming year; a number of these products have completed customer validation and will move into production in the coming months
- Current order visibility indicates the export recovery is expected to continue through 2026, driven by pre-buy activity ahead of upcoming emission-related regulatory changes
